ticket.title: Automated Greetings Incorrectly Recognize Honorifics as First Names
ticket.description:
#### Customer Name

Name 29

#### Customer Email

<email>

#### Workspace name

Name 29

#### Screenshot

 <image> 

#### What are you trying to achieve?

Ensure Acquisity correctly identifies users' first names when generating automated greetings, including accounts registered with professional titles such as Dr., Mr., Mrs., Ms., or Prof.

#### What are you doing to achieve it?

The customer originally registered his Acquisity account with the name "Dr Name 29," which caused the platform to address him as "Hi Dr!"

He has since manually updated his profile to "Name 31" as a workaround.

#### What is happening instead?

Acquisity currently interprets the first word of a user's full name as their first name without accounting for honorifics.

Name 32 has already updated his profile, the underlying issue remains relevant to other users.

The previous investigation under ENG-2624 identified 12 additional accounts with similar naming issues, affecting 13 accounts in total.

#### What is the expected outcome?

Acquisity should automatically recognize and exclude common honorifics when generating personalized greetings.

For example:

"Dr Name 29" → "Hi Name 33!"

"Mr Name 34" → "Hi Name 34!"

This should prevent future users from needing to manually remove titles from their profile names.

Previous investigation:
<url:Name 30.app>

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR automated reply signs off with wrong/hallucinated name (mismatch with sending mailbox)
relatedSnapshot.description:
BUG: Yes EVIDENCE: * Customer: Name 3 (), workspace "Name 3' Workspace" (org ). * An automated AI SDR reply was sent FROM the warmed mailbox `` (From name renders "Name 4") but was SIGNED "Wilder". * Prod DB confirms this is real, not a display glitch: crm_message `` (thread ``) body_html = `

Hi Name 5,

Got it, I'll reach out to you at .

Best,
Wilder

`. metadata.isManualReply=false, isAutoReply=false → automated copywriter path (NOT a manual escalation takeover). * The SAME wrong name "Wilder" also appears on a second automated reply in the same workspace sent from a DIFFERENT mailbox `` (thread ``). Both were replies to auto/out-of-office responses. * "Wilder" appears nowhere in the workspace's AI SDR knowledge base, ai_sdr_setting, outreach_provider settings, campaign variants, or members (only member is Name 3) → the name is fabricated at generation time. ROOT CAUSE: * The automated reply is generated by the AI SDR v2 copywriter. Its prompt (`apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/agents/copywriter/default-agent.ts`) instructs the model to "Use the sender name from context (extract from the first email signature or email address if needed)." * But the copywriter context never includes the sending mailbox's sender name. Thread history is built by `getThreadHistory` (`apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/normalization-shared.ts`) and formatted by `formatThreadHistory` (`apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/workflow/helpers/context-pack.ts`) as `[SDR]`/`[PROSPECT]` + body only — no from_name/sender field. Outbound (SDR) crm_message bodies are empty in our records (Company One outbound bodies aren't stored), so the original email's `{{sendingAccountName}}` signature isn't available to extract either. * With no sender name in context, the LLM hallucinates a sign-off ("Wilder"). `finalize.ts`/`send-email.ts` do no signature correction. POTENTIAL FIX: * Pass the sending mailbox's sender name (the Company One sending-account display/first name, e.g. "Name 6") explicitly into the copywriter context pack and instruct the model to use it for the sign-off, instead of asking it to extract from an (empty) email body. This mirrors the fix already shipped for the manual/escalation path in ENG-11322 (used inbox alias name for sign-off), which does NOT cover this automated copywriter path. WHATS NEEDED TO RESOLVE: * Resolve the sending-account/mailbox sender name at reply-generation time (from the outreach provider / Company One account or the campaign sending account) and thread it into the copywriter context; update the copywriter prompt to sign off with that name. Add a guard so replies never sign with a name absent from the sender identity. RELATED: * ENG-11322 (Done) — manual escalation-takeover replies; same class of mismatch but different (manual) code path. * ENG-7297 (old, duplicate/archived, v1) — "AISDR shows [sender] instead of actual name". INTERCOM: SLACK THREAD: DEVIN SESSION:

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer report: first-name-only CSV import leaves combined first and last name in the campaign leads table
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Contact: Name 7 (<email>) · workspace: Company Four (owner)

Bounded context: Customer imported a CSV containing only first names into a cold email campaign, then reported that the campaign's Leads table still shows first and last name together in one "Name" column. She had earlier exported a campaign CSV and removed the last-name column, and the campaign was already launched.

Finding (Platform Limitation, not a defect):

* Every leads table (campaign Leads tab, manually uploaded leads, workspace leads) renders a single "Name" column defined as full name, else first name + last name joined. The help center documents this: "Name | First and last name combined". There is no first-name-only display.
* On import, a lead that already exists in the workspace keep its stored names for any field the uploaded row leaves blank, so a first-name-only file does not clear a last name that is already stored on the existing lead record. Verified in code (bulk campaign-lead persistence: resolvedFirstName/resolvedLastName fall back to the existing lead/pool row) and in production: the affected campaign's imported leads all correspond to workspace lead records created earlier, and no new lead records were created during the import, yet the imported leads all carry last names.
* Mapping and the CSV are not at fault: the first-name column maps correctly, the stored first-name field holds only the first name, and {{firstName}} personalisation renders the first name only.

Open human action: reply to the customer in Intercom explaining the combined Name column and that last names cannot be cleared by re-importing; to show only a first name on a lead, clear its Last name via Edit Lead (affects future sends only). Reopens if the customer's CSV column mapped to the name field is shown to contain full names.

Bounded summary for resume: one live Intercom conversation, product/feedback lane, no money ask.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add a sender first name variable to email and text templates
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Why

Close templates say "it's {{ user.first_name }} from AI Acquisition". Acquisity only offers `{{sender.name}}`, the sender's full name, so the imported AI Acquisition Sales Team templates now read "it's Name 8" instead of "it's Name 9".

## What

Add `{{sender.first_name}}` ("Sender first name") to the variable picker for email and text templates and composers. It is the first word of the same sender name `{{sender.name}}` uses today. An empty sender name behaves like any missing variable: the send is blocked unless the template has a fallback.

Name 10 possible change: the variable catalogue entry, one value in the render endpoint, and a unit test. No schema, no UI component changes.

## Done when

- [ ] "Sender first name" appears in the variable picker.
- [ ] A template with `{{sender.first_name}}` previews and sends with the sender's first name.
- [ ] Unit test covers the first-name split, including extra spaces and an empty name.

## Follow-up after merge

Switch the 45 imported Sales Team templates from `{{sender.name}}` to `{{sender.first_name}}` where Close used the first name (pack: `~/Documents/CRM/close-templates-2026-09-29/`).

relatedSnapshot.title: Store and preserve separate first and last names
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

People keep separate first and last names while showing their full name throughout the CRM. Reps can sort by surname, and names arriving from imports, integrations and Cold Email Agent retain the parts already known about the person.

## User experience

Creating or editing a person shows First name and Last name. Tables and record headers still show Full name by default; first and last names can also be added as columns, filters and export fields. New full-name-only input is retained as first name with last name empty. Existing records are not automatically rewritten.

## What's included

* Add nullable first/last columns while keeping the existing full-name column compatible with current consumers and public API cursors.
* Preserve structured names through manual edits, people/company/deal CSV imports, single/batch public API requests, workflow create/update/upsert/merge, outreach webhooks, AI SDR, Calendly/native bookings and other inventoried intake writers.
* Cold Email Agent → AI SDR → CRM passes real first/last values directly. SDR prompt context also exposes those parts; no AI name parser or join-then-split round trip.
* Full-name display, existing search matches, separate name filters, surname sorting and selected-column exports. Missing surnames sort last in either direction, with deterministic tie-breakers.
* Coherent name selection during merge, preserving existing ownership, relationships and side effects.

Name 11 mapping verified on 14 September: the active registration workflow already receives separate first_name/last_name but concatenates them into name. Carry the original parts directly; do not add a guessing parser. Attendance and payment workflows currently supply full names only.

## How it should work

Structured parts take precedence over a conflicting submitted display name. Omission preserves values; explicit clearing is distinct. An unchanged echoed full name preserves existing parts. Placeholder names derived from email/phone or “Unknown” remain display-only. Existing SDR-matched people retain their CRM names; background sync must not become a backfill.

Deploy additive schema and compatible writers first. During mixed versions, name-only inserts remain legacy/null, and a database guard clears stale parts on a legacy-only rename rather than guessing them. Structured edits are enabled only after old writers drain. Do not rewrite existing records globally.

## Done when

- [ ] First/last names survive all inventoried write families and appear consistently in full-name displays, queries, API responses and exports.
- [ ] Tests cover multi-word given/surnames, first-only, last-only, legacy-only, placeholders, explicit clears, stale full-name echoes, conflicting source values and merge tuple selection.
- [ ] Separate name filters and surname sorting work in saved views; old views and API pagination remain compatible.
- [ ] Migration and mixed-version tests prove no global backfill and no stale parts after legacy writes.
- [ ] The verified webinar registration mapping passes source first_name/last_name directly through crm/upsert-contact after deployment, preserving email matching, deal fields and the validated fill-empty phone chain. Full-name-only attendance/payment mappings and unchanged-name echoes are covered by regression tests.
- [ ] Browser QA covers create/edit, inline/full-name display, saved views, sort, import preview, export and merge. UI designs will be attached when James completes them; reconcile the final controls with those designs before UI sign-off.
- [ ] Activation tracking uses the repository instrumentation skill and is verified in PostHog without personal name data in events.

## References

Reconstructing name parts after they have already been supplied loses information and produces incorrect greetings. Name 12 and Name 13 expose first/last/full values; Close uses separate name parts in templates. This feature deliberately leaves legacy rows untouched, with one separately reviewed workspace exception.

Relate to historical people ownership/name scope, completed CSV name mapping, and deal/person parity. Do not reopen or broaden those issues automatically.

## Delivery order and design status

Pickup rank 1; earliest dependency wave 1. No feature-ticket blocker. Pick up names first; serialize shared CRM schema/migration edits with personal-template work.

James is designing the UI. Create and plan this ticket now; attach the matching designs later. Backend/data work can proceed. Final visible controls must follow the completed designs before UI sign-off. CRM redesign handover.

## Implementation context

AI context.md contains the reviewed data contract, source inventory, live webinar mapping and required verification.

relatedSnapshot.title: [Email Bison] Sequences — Bug: Subject line saves incorrectly on paused campaign (duplicate first name variable)
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

When editing a subject line on a paused campaign in Email Bison, saving causes the subject line to contain two first name variables. Removing the duplicate first name variable and saving causes it to reappear.

This was reproduced **3 times** — the duplicate variable reappears after every save.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a paused campaign in Email Bison
2. Edit the subject line
3. Save — subject line now contains two first name variables
4. Remove the duplicate first name variable
5. Save again — the duplicate reappears

## Name 19

* Subject lines save correctly with the exact value entered
* No variables are duplicated on save

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Subject lines save correctly on paused campaigns without duplicating variables
- [ ] Editing and saving a subject line persists the exact value entered
- [ ] No variable duplication occurs regardless of campaign status (active, paused, draft)

relatedSnapshot.title: Add support for first name and last name in CSV import
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Context

Currently, the CSV import feature only supports mapping one "File column" to one CRM property. Since our CRM has a single "Name" property instead of separate "First Name" and "Last Name" fields, users cannot import data where first and last names are in separate columns.

## Problem

Many data sources have first name and last name as separate columns, but our current import system cannot handle this split format.

## Proposed Solution (from Name 12's approach)

Implement two solutions:

1. **Without changing the database table**: Split the name into first name and last name in the frontend, then join them while saving in the backend
2. **With database changes**: Create 2 separate database columns for first name and last name

The first approach is simpler and cleaner, as demonstrated in Name 23's implementation.

## Screenshots

See attached screenshots showing the current mapping limitation.
